To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) structural abnormality of resistance small arteries, measured as the media:lumen ratio (M:L) is associated with cardiovascular events in essential (primary) hypertensive patients; (2) this relationship is independent from other cardiovascular risk factors, such as the Heart Score (10-year cardiovascular mortality risk estimate); and (3) this association is independent from the presence or absence of diabetes.

increased M: L of resistance arteries, a structural abnormality that is characteristic of essential hypertension and that has previously been associated with increased cardiovascular risk in patients with diabetes, is also an independent predictor of future cardiovascular events in patients with uncomplicated essential hypertension.
the M: L is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease in essential hypertension.
